Move points off the empty cells of a grid

Source: R/snap_to_valid_cell.R
snap_to_valid_cell.Rd

Finds the locations that fall in a cell with no value and moves each to the centre of the nearest cell that has one, within radius_deg, leaving every other location untouched. Intended for land-only grids — ERA5-Land is a land model on a 0.1 degree grid, GloFAS stops at the coast — where a household on land can sit in an empty cell.

Usage

snap_to_valid_cell(
  x,
  raster,
  radius_deg = 0.25,
  lat = lat,
  lon = lon,
  layer = 1
)

Arguments

x

A data frame with coordinate columns, or a table from prepare_coord().

raster

A SpatRaster, or a file path. Only layer is looked at: the cells a land mask leaves empty are the same on every date.

radius_deg

How far a point may be moved, in degrees, converted at 111 320 m per degree. The default 0.25 is two and a half cells of the 0.1 degree ERA5-Land grid.

lat, lon

<tidy-select> Coordinate columns; lat and lon by default.

layer

Which layer to read the empty cells from.

Value

x with the coordinates of the moved points replaced, and a snapped column: TRUE where the point was moved, FALSE where it was already in a cell with a value or no cell was near enough. The original coordinates are kept in lat_given and lon_given.

Details

Nearest rather than interpolated, and bounded, so a moved point reads one real neighbouring cell's value and cannot take one from across the country. A location further than radius_deg from any cell with a value is left where it is, and reads NA: the usual reason is that it is genuinely offshore.

fill_missing_rast() does the same job on the raster, by a focal mean over the neighbours rather than by taking one of them. Prefer that when the raster is the thing to keep, and this when the points are: filling a forty-year daily stack to change the value of a handful of locations interpolates some fifteen thousand layers to no purpose.

See also

fill_missing_rast(), extract_by_coord()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pre <- read_climate(files, variable = "pre")
places |>
    snap_to_valid_cell(pre) |>
    prepare_coord(lat, lon, id = place)
} # }
